title: Outlook: choose unread or total item count for each folder in the folder pane
summary: The roadmap facts and the absence of documented administrator controls check out. The cost rating needs correction: the sources establish Outlook's licensing requirements but do not explicitly establish that this option has no additional cost.

claims.claim: Users choose unread count or total item count separately for each folder.
claims.quote: You can now pick whether each folder in your folder pane shows the unread count or the total item count.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The choice is made by right-clicking a folder and choosing total or unread count.
claims.quote: Just right-click any folder and choose whether to show the total or unread count.

claims.claim: The roadmap says Outlook previously displayed only unread counts.
claims.quote: Until now, Outlook only displayed unread counts, but sometimes you need to see how many items are in a folder overall.

claims.quote: It gives you more control over how you keep track of your email without changing how anything else works.

claims.claim: Outlook on the web must be enabled for mailboxes whose users are to receive new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: As a requirement, Outlook on the web needs to be enabled for users' mailboxes for whom you're planning to deploy new Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration configures per-mailbox Outlook on the web display settings, some of which also apply to new Outlook.
claims.quote: These settings are applied in Outlook on the web only. Some settings also apply to the new Outlook client.

claims.claim: MailFolderPaneExpanded is a real Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration parameter for an Outlook on the web folder pane setting.
claims.quote: Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration ... [-MailFolderPaneExpanded <Boolean>] ... [-NavigationPaneViewOption <NavigationPaneView>]

claims.claim: The change is a user-chosen count display difference rather than a roadmap-described change to other behaviour.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cost rating is none despite the absence of an explicit statement that this option is included without additional cost.
claims.quote: cost: "none"; "None. An option inside Outlook that comes with the licence Outlook already needs" versus "Microsoft publishes no separate licence, meter or charge for this option. The only cost the sources show is the time to tell helpdesk staff about it."
claims.fix: Set cost to low. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Low. The known cost is helpdesk communication time; Microsoft has not published a separate price or meter for this option.' Keep the product-level licensing model included, but do not use the absence of a published charge to assert no additional cost.
